Subject: Question on billing rounding for mixed short/long streams

Hi Jonas,

Quick question from procurement as we finish the SOW: our application makes a mix of very short completion calls (2–8 tokens of output) and occasional long-context generation (10k+ tokens) interleaved in the same session. The finance team is worried about how those requests will be billed when they land in the same conversation: do short calls get rounded to the per-call minimum independently, or are they aggregated into the session/context bucket and billed at amortized units?

We saw reference to "context amortization" in the draft pricing schedule but it's not concrete. Can you confirm the rounding behavior and whether there is any minimum billing floor that will apply to those short bursts when they are part of a long-running conversation? Also, does KV cache reuse reduce the per-token billable units for the long calls?

We'd like a short written answer that we can attach to the purchase order. Thanks — Alyssa

Alyssa — thanks for the clear question. Short answer up front: short completions are first evaluated for aggregation into the active conversation bucket (if the session meets active-context criteria). If the call is a stand-alone per-call request or a short burst that does not meet the active-context aggregation window, it will hit the minimum per-call quantum. For your use case (interleaved short bursts inside a persistent long conversation), we generally amortize short bursts into the conversation-level accounting when they share the same conversation_id and occur within the configured aggregation window.

I'm looping in Kim and Sergio from Billing/Platform to provide the exact math and an example invoice line so you can attach it to the PO. I'll also include a short calc workbook.

Subject: Re: Question on billing rounding for mixed short/long streams

Jonas — details below and attaching sample_calcs_hybrid-rounding.xlsx.

Platform policy (current default):
- Aggregation window: 30 minutes of activity on the same conversation_id (configurable on Dedicated/Private tiers).
- If multiple calls fall inside the window they are considered for "conversation amortization." Billable units are computed on the conversation's total billable tokens first, then rounded up to the quantum (default quantum = 1 token for hosted; for committed SKUs there may be a minimum 100-token slab policy).
- Stand-alone per-call requests that cannot be attributed to an active conversation are evaluated against the per-call minimum (default: min_charge = 10 tokens for per-call SKU).
- Rounding: we round per-invoice-line after aggregation. Example: conversation total billable tokens = 11,015.3 -> invoice rounds up to 11,016 tokens. Short calls aggregated into that conversation are not separately bumped to per-call minimums.
- KV cache/prefix reuse: KV reuse reduces compute and can reduce the effective per-token cost on Dedicated/Private (we apply a "% compute credit" to committed invoices when KV hit rate > 20%). It does not change the raw tokenization/metric used for billable token counts — those remain based on model-visible tokens. We do, however, apply usage credits to the invoice as a separate line-item for KV efficiency in committed deals.

Sample calc (from workbook):
- Long generation: 11,000 output tokens + 50 input tokens -> 11,050 billable tokens
- Short replies (3 x 5 output tokens + small input): 3 x 8 billable tokens = 24 tokens
- Conversation total = 11,074 tokens -> invoice rounds to 11,074 (no extra per-call minimums for the shorts since aggregated)
- If the short replies had been isolated per-call requests (no active conversation_id within window), they'd each be billed as max(8, per-call-min=10) -> 3 x 10 = 30 tokens (worse for you)

Attached: sample_calcs_hybrid-rounding.xlsx (contains step-by-step math and a toggled example for committed slab minima). Also added a short draft amendment (draft_amendment_ACME_v2.pdf) language we can include in the SOW to make the aggregation window explicit (suggested: 30 min default, can set to 10/60 min by request).

Let me know if you want us to bake the 30-minute aggregation window into the SOW as a firm term for Acme's Dedicated commitment.

Subject: Final clarity for PO — hybrid-context rounding and KV reuse credits

Alyssa — following internal confirmation, here is a short formal statement you can attach to the PO: 

1) Aggregation and rounding: when requests share the same conversation_id and occur within a 30-minute activity window, they are aggregated and billed on the conversation total. The invoice will reflect the aggregated token total rounded to the next whole token or committed quantum per your SKU. Short bursts aggregated in this way are not subject to separate per-call minimums.

2) Stand-alone calls: any request that is not attributable to an active conversation within the aggregation window is evaluated against the per-call minimum for the SKU in use (default per-call minimum = 10 tokens for hosted per-call pricing; committed SKUs may have different slab minima).

3) KV cache/prefix reuse: KV cache hits do not change the token counting algorithm; they can reduce effective compute cost. For Dedicated/Committed deals Redwood will apply a compute-efficiency credit to the invoice when KV hit rate exceeds the agreed threshold. That credit appears as a separate invoice line item and does not change the reported billable token quantity.
